Harry Halliday (born **1855**, died **1922**) was an English cricketer who played primarily for **Lancashire** and **Oxford University** in the late 19th century. Here’s everything known about him:

---

### **1. Early Life & Education**
- **Full Name**: Henry Halliday (commonly known as Harry Halliday).
- **Born**: **1855** (exact date unknown) in **Liverpool, England**.
- **Education**: Attended **Liverpool College** before going up to **Brasenose College, Oxford**, where he played cricket for the university.

---

### **2. Cricket Career**
#### **First-Class Debut**
- Made his first-class debut for **Oxford University** in **1876** against the **MCC** at Lord’s.
- Played **32 first-class matches** between **1876 and 1883**, primarily for:
  - **Oxford University** (1876–1878)
  - **Lancashire** (1878–1883)
  - **MCC** (occasional appearances)

#### **Batting Style**
- **Right-handed batsman** (position in the order varied, often in the middle order).
- Known for his **defensive technique** and **solidity** rather than aggressive strokeplay.
- **Highest first-class score**: **103** (for Oxford University vs. Gentlemen of England, **1878**).
- **Career batting average**: **18.36** (modest by modern standards but respectable for the era).

#### **Bowling & Fielding**
- **Right-arm fast-medium bowler** (occasional bowler, not a frontline option).
- Took **10 first-class wickets** at an average of **28.50**.
- **Fielding**: Primarily a **slip fielder**, though no records suggest he was exceptional in the field.

#### **Notable Performances**
- **1878**: Scored his only first-class century (**103**) for Oxford University against the Gentlemen of England at **The Oval**.
- **1880**: Played for Lancashire against **Australia** (the first Australian touring team in England), scoring **32 and 15**.
- **1881**: Took his best bowling figures (**4/30**) for Lancashire against **Yorkshire** at **Old Trafford**.

#### **End of Career**
- Last first-class match: **1883** (for Lancashire vs. Gloucestershire).
- After retiring, he remained involved in cricket as a **club cricketer** and possibly an administrator.

---

### **3. Personal Life & Later Years**
- **Occupation**: Likely worked in **business or commerce** (common for amateur cricketers of the era).
- **Death**: **1922** (exact date and place unknown).
- **Legacy**: A **solid county cricketer** of his time, though not a household name. His century for Oxford remains his standout achievement.

---

### **4. Statistical Summary (First-Class Career)**
| **Category**       | **Details**                     |
|--------------------|---------------------------------|
| **Matches**        | 32                              |
| **Runs**           | 955                             |
| **Highest Score**  | 103                             |
| **Average**        | 18.36                           |
| **100s/50s**       | 1/3                             |
| **Wickets**        | 10                              |
| **Best Bowling**   | 4/30                            |
| **Catches**        | 12                              |

---

### **5. Context in Cricket History**
- Played in the **pre-Test match era** (England’s first Test was in **1877**, but Halliday never represented his country).
- The **1870s–1880s** were a transitional period in cricket, with **overarm bowling** becoming standard and **county cricket** expanding.
- Lancashire was a **strong county side** in this period, with players like **A.N. Hornby** and **Dick Barlow** (of "Lancashire's famous pair" fame) as contemporaries.

---

### **6. Possible Confusions & Clarifications**
- **Not to be confused with**:
  - **Harry Halliday (footballer)** (a different person, active in the early 20th century).
  - **Other Hallidays** in cricket (e.g., **George Halliday**, a 19th-century Surrey player).
- **No known relation** to modern cricketers with the same surname.

---

### **7. Sources & Further Reading**
- **CricketArchive**: [Harry Halliday’s profile](https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/) (requires subscription).
- **Wisden Cricketers' Almanack**: May have brief mentions in obituaries or match reports.
- **Lancashire CCC archives**: For county-specific details.
- **Oxford University Cricket Club records**: For his university career.

---

### **8. Why Isn’t He Better Known?**
- **Amateur status**: Many cricketers of his era were amateurs who played for love of the game rather than as professionals.
- **Modest statistics**: His average and record don’t stand out compared to legends like **W.G. Grace** or **Alfred Shaw**.
- **Lack of Test cricket**: Never played for England (Tests were rare and selective in his time).

---

### **Final Thoughts**
Harry Halliday was a **reliable county cricketer** who contributed to Lancashire and Oxford University during a formative period in English cricket. While not a superstar, his century for Oxford and his role in Lancashire’s team make him a notable figure in **19th-century cricket history**.
